title: Two Pointers: Solve This Interview Question in O(n) (Java) | DSA #2 #shorts
description:
Find two numbers in a sorted array that add up to a target. The brute-force way checks every pair: O(n²). The two-pointer trick puts one pointer at each end. If the sum is too small, move the left pointer right; if it's too big, move the right pointer left. Each step throws away a number that can't be part of the answer, so it finishes in a single pass: O(n) time, O(1) extra space.

lines: Find two numbers in a sorted array that add up to a target. Most people check every pair.
Checking every pair is O(n²). A million numbers means half a trillion checks.
Instead, put one pointer at the start, and one at the end, and add them up.
Too small? Move the left pointer right, to a bigger number. Too big? Move the right pointer left. Each step rules out a number for good.
When the sum hits the target, you're done. One pass through the array: O(n) time, and no extra memory.
